The script was written without a storyboard, and the first draft fell short

The storyboard step truncated at max_tokens, and the pipeline fell back to writing the script with no storyboard at all. The script therefore ran unplanned. The first draft came in at 3088 words against a target of 3400, and was sent back for one expand pass. The shipped script is 3662 words, above target, so the expand pass overshot. The unplanned script still matched citations well: 12 of 18 roundup citations and 4 of 5 deep-dive citations. Where the storyboard is truncating, the fix belongs in the storyboard step's max_tokens setting, since that is the step that failed.

Six TTS takes returned shorter than their word counts predicted, and each was retried once. Four of the retries were still short. The longer take of each pair was kept, so the audio carries the full script. The four still-short takes mean the synthesis returned less audio than the text required, even on retry, and this is worth watching if the count rises on future nights.

The roundup cut 11 stories, as designed, while the deep dives held at five

The airtime budget dropped 11 stories from the roundup pool, which the pipeline is built to do. The deep-dive count was 5. This is the normal split between the two segments, and no change is indicated.

What happened

Script shipped 335 words under target after a single expand pass

The first draft came in at 3015 words against a target of 3400. It was sent back once for an expand pass, and what shipped was 3735 words, which is over target. The gap was closed, but only one pass was allowed, so the final figure is the result of that one retry rather than a second check against the target.

The 3735 figure is the number that matters for the length threshold. A thin day shipping under target is intended behaviour; if this night's length is a problem, it would show against SHORT_EPISODE_WORDS, and no such finding appears here. Nothing needs changing on this count.

Roundup dropped 22 stories to fit the airtime budget

The roundup pool was larger than one segment could air, so 22 stories were cut by the airtime budget set at NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT. The pool is designed to run larger than the airtime, and a cut story can come back on a day where it matches better. These stories are not lost to the archive.

Of the 18 roundup citations in the script, 13 matched their source. The five unmatched citations are the only citation gap in the run. The four deep-dive citations all matched. If the unmatched roundup citations need checking, that is the place to look.

Personality clue extraction failed on the host-memory step

The persist-host-memory step failed with an unterminated string at line 1, column 548. The personality clue extraction was skipped, so the hosts' memory of this episode was not updated from the script. The episode itself shipped and the listener heard it as normal.

The effect shows up later, when the hosts are expected to recall clues from this episode and cannot. Fix the JSON emitted by the host-memory step, because the extractor only fails when its input is malformed.

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific, on time, and completed successfully, finishing at 1:34 AM Pacific. Fallback 1 at 2:05 AM Pacific also completed successfully with no delay. Fallback 2 at 3:05 AM Pacific is the run producing this review and is still in progress. The scheduler chain fired as designed, but the primary run was the only one whose output was needed.

The first draft came in at 2,536 words against a target of 3,400, so it was sent back for one expand pass. The shipped script is 3,529 words, which is above target, not under it. The expand pass overshot the target by 129 words, so the length control is loose in the upward direction as well as the downward one. The editorial review does not treat this as a failure, but the one-pass rule is what let it land above target.

What happened

The script shipped at 3955 words, well above the 3400-word target

The first draft came in at 3158 words against a 3400 target, so it was sent back for up to two expand passes. The script that shipped ran to 3955 words, 555 over target. Read the drafts with that in mind: the expansion added length rather than correcting a shortfall the listener would have heard.

Casey carried 52% of the deep-dive words and spoke at a 1.14 ratio over Riley. The pipeline does not balance hosts by word count, so this is the default behaviour showing through, not a fault. Check whether the expand prompt is steering toward whichever host is already ahead.

Eleven of the 18 roundup citations matched their sources, and 3 of the 4 deep-dive citations matched. The roundup gap is the weaker point: seven roundup citations did not align with their stories. Whether the seven misaligned citations come from the stories that aired or from the pool is not separated in the figures.

Tighten the citation check in the roundup stage so that a mismatch is caught before the script is written, not after.

Debate question asks who controls mining benefit and whether local standing gives a say

The debate question for the day was: who actually holds control and benefit from mining and processing ventures, and does local standing (crews, ranch families, Indigenous claims) translate into a real say in outcomes? The four deep dives covered Chile's refining bottleneck, the Seville panel on European mining support, the Sudan strike that killed at least 72 miners, and China's Argentina footprint. The question was broad enough to take all four, which is why the selection held together.

What happened

The script shipped 3272 words against a 3400 target after two expand passes

The first draft came in at 2879 words, under the 3400-word target, and was sent back for up to two expand passes. The shipped script is 3272 words, still short of target. The expansion recovered most of the gap but not all of it, and the episode runs at 19.8 minutes of audio.

Lower the target word count or the expand threshold in the script stage if a 3400-word target is meant to be met on most nights. Otherwise leave it, since the gap is small.

Four stories were cut from the roundup pool by the airtime budget

The roundup pool is larger than one segment can air, so 24 stories were dropped by NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT. This is by design: a cut story can resurface on a better-matched day.

Two sources disagree on citations. Of the 18 roundup citations, 14 matched; of the 4 deep-dive citations, 3 matched. Check the unmatched citations before trusting the roundup attributions on this episode.

One AI-tell pattern hit reached the shipped script

The quality check recorded one AI-tell pattern hit in the final script. Casey's share of the voice ratio against Riley is 0.92, and Casey carries 48% of the deep-dive word count.

If the AI-tell hit recurs on consecutive nights, add the matched phrase to the banned list in the script prompt.
